correctness.rationale: Applying the Hatori--Oi stability theorem to a bijection and its inverse gives two bounded positive linear asymptotic cores. Scaling the uniformly bounded errors at na forces their compositions to be the identity. The c0 phase-transition formula follows from an exact two-slope scalar inverse calculation.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Hatori--Oi already provide the one-sided linear core, its dense-range counterexample, and an order-isomorphism conclusion under a different coarse lower-distance hypothesis. No source found states the two-sided finite-defect equivalence, exact mutual-inverse core identification, or the weighted c0 inverse-defect formula. An unpublished related Hatori--Oi manuscript remains a residual source risk.

value.rationale: The result pinpoints the structural boundary behind the newly exhibited loss of surjectivity: inverse finite FM defect is exactly equivalent to bounded order-isomorphic linearization, and a weighted c0 family makes the transition quantitative with inverse defect epsilon/inf(w_n).

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
